title: Disentangling reproductive history and parenthood in late-life cognitive and vascular brain health
title_zh: 解构晚年认知与脑血管健康中的生殖史与育儿
abstract: Women bear a greater burden of Alzheimer's disease (AD), prompting interest in whether reproductive history contributes to late-life brain health. Yet parity, a count of live births, compresses biologically and socially distinct reproductive trajectories into a single measure. Current human biomarker studies provide little evidence that parity tracks amyloid-β or tau pathology. The clearest human evidence links adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs), particularly hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), to later vascular brain injury and vascular dementia, supporting a life-course vascular framework that separates preconception susceptibility, pregnancy complications, and postpartum recovery. Mother-father comparisons further indicate that parenthood-related social exposures contribute to the observed associations. Obstetric history therefore has direct relevance to vascular risk assessment, whereas AD biomarker testing should follow established clinical and biomarker indications rather than parity. Future studies should pair exposure-resolved reproductive histories with serial postpartum phenotyping, vascular neuroimaging, and longitudinal AD biomarkers.
abstract_zh: 女性患阿尔茨海默病（AD）的风险更高，这促使人们关注生殖史是否影响晚年脑健康。然而，生育次数将在生物学和社会学方面截然不同的生殖轨迹浓缩为单一指标。目前的人类生物标志物研究几乎没有证据表明生育次数能追踪淀粉样β或tau病理。最明确的人类证据将不良妊娠结局（APO），特别是妊娠期高血压疾病（HDP），与晚年脑血管损伤和血管性痴呆联系起来，支持一种将先孕期易感性、妊娠并发症和产后恢复分开的生命过程血管框架。母父比较进一步表明，与育儿相关的社会暴露有助于解释上述关联。因此，产科史对血管风险评估具有直接意义，而AD生物标志物检测应遵循既定的临床和生物标志物指标，而非生育次数。未来的研究应将解析后的生殖史与产后丰富的随访表型、脑血管成像和AD生物标志物相结合。
